title.narrative: PRO-RESILIENCE: Promoting climate resilient urban development in the city of Beira

description.narrative:
DESCRIPTION The herein project, aims to respond to the exposure to multi-dimensional risks faced by the city of Beira, in central region of Mozambique, due to the increasing impact of climate change, exposure to natural hazards, vulnerability of infrastructure and rapid urbanization. Together with the Municipal council, UN-Habitat developed a proposal which, by the inclusion of local government representants, community and relevant stakeholders, aim at defining a Strategic Development Framework (SDF), to be applied as guideline for next interventions and coordination tool for partners-supported implementations. The SDF will be the reference and baseline for the slum upgrading pilot experience in the informal settlement area within the Chipangara neighboorhood, where will be developed a Detailed plan (Plano de Pormenor – PP) implemented partially through pilot catalytic infrastructures.
APPROACH To address the multi-dimensional vulnerabilities affecting the city of Beira and exposing their built and human environment to the effects of climate change, working from the planning dimension to the materialization of quick local impacts through pilot initiatives, the project will use the Our City Plan participatory approach, a global toolbox developed by UN-Habitat that guides and supports local governments and urban actors to understand, customize, and develop comprehensive, inclusive, and integrated urban planning processes towards sustainable urban development and increased resilience. This approach is structured into four phases: Phase 1: Assessment The first phase focuses on collecting and analyzing data at city level and at Chipangara neighborhood level, based on existing instruments, such as the Urban structure Plan (PEU) and the Building Resilience and Recovery Programme (BRRP). Meetings with the local government play a central role in identifying available human and physical resources, as well as understanding the urban and socioeconomic context. This process includes workshops to assess local government capacities, stakeholder mapping, and the integration of desk research (e.g., existing GIS data, plans, and studies) and field research (utilizing tools like Kobo Collect). A climate and vulnerability assessment, followed by community-based participatory workshop, is also conducted to identify key climate-related challenges – and possible solutions – faced by the community. The first phase results in the development of a guiding document outlining an operational work plan, key team members of the Technical Working Group (TWG), and the tools and strategies to be applied throughout the project. Participatory spatial analysis, incremental mapping, and diagnostic exercises are carried out to identify vulnerabilities and sensitivities to environmental risks, supported by spatial and statistical analysis. Findings are summarized in a comprehensive analysis report, validated through a Diagnostic Workshop. Phase 2: Planning This phase focuses on defining a common vision through participatory activities and developing strategic plans at both city and neighbourhood/community level, focusing on Chipangara as prioritized area. The key output of this phase, the Strategic Development Framework (SDF) and the related Plan, outlines main objectives, targets, and priority actions, complete with indicators and linkages to global frameworks such as the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the New Urban Agenda (NUA). The plan includes pilot projects designed to address the identified challenges through and community based interventions, maximizing the impact on skills development, income generation and employment. Addressing multiple issues across different areas simultaneously, allows for the identification of common elements and response strategies, reducing the scale and number of required interventions. The planning phase counts with a strategic visioning workshop to spatialize a shared vision for Beira City and participatory activities to validate and promote the Strategic Development Plan. At the neighborhood level, a participatory design process is used to create the Chipangara Neighborhood Plan. This plan will include analysis, mapping, sensitization and policy/norms development regarding the thematic of housing land and property, security of tenure and will be the baseline for the elaboration of ToRs and a roadmap for the development of a Detailed Plan (PP) for the target area, as land management instrument approved by the MozambiqueTerritorial Management Law. Along these initiatives, the sustainable actions to address climate-related and urban challenges are collected and organized in a Climate Resilient Living Manual by a consultant. The manual should be validated by the Technical Working Group (TWG) to ensure alignment with the project’s vision and objectives.
